definitions.explanation: A plain white flag used as a symbol of surrender, truce, or ceasefire. Also used figuratively to mean giving up.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}が{白旗|しらはた}を{振|ふ}って{降伏|こうふく}した。
examples.english: The enemy waved a white flag and surrendered.

examples.japanese: あまりにも{難|むずか}しい{問題|もんだい}だったので、{白旗|しらはた}を{上|あ}げてしまった。
examples.english: The problem was so difficult that I gave up.

notes:
{白旗|しらはた} is a white flag used as a universal symbol of surrender, truce, or ceasefire. It is also used figuratively in everyday Japanese to mean giving up or admitting defeat. The word can also be read しろはた, but しらはた is the standard reading.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {白旗|しらはた}を{上|あ}げる: to raise a white flag; to surrender
- {白旗|しらはた}を{振|ふ}る: to wave a white flag

The expression {白旗|しらはた}を{上|あ}げる is frequently used figuratively to mean giving up on a task or challenge.

RELATED WORDS:
- {赤旗|あかはた}: red flag (danger signal, or the communist flag)
- {旗印|はたじるし}: banner; rallying symbol
